data.cultural_impact: Fitrah is a fundamental concept in Islamic culture, representing the essential human nature that is indivisible from the faith. It highlights the importance of remaining true to our personal beliefs and ethics, even in the face of opposing societal pressures. This idea is reiterated during the celebration of Eid al-Fitr, which commemorates the end of the holy month of Ramadan. Muslims around the world come together to perform the Eid prayer and engage in acts of charity, emphasizing the unity of spirit and the common thread of human nature that connects us all.

By adhering to our Fitrah and nurturing our inherent beliefs in monotheism and submission to God, we are able to build a strong spiritual foundation and deepen our connection with the divine. This concept also underlines the importance of personal responsibility in our spiritual journey, as we are guided by our own conscience, rather than relying on external sources or external influence. Fitrah serves as a reminder of our ultimate purpose in life and encourages us to constantly strive towards self-improvement and closeness to God.
